clue.text: Gland found in healthy muscular tissue ?

indicators.note: found in says the letters are sitting inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A gland is discovered lurking in someone's fit, muscular body.
explanation.definitionFit: The thymus is a gland in the chest behind the breastbone, important in the immune system.

clue.text: Old painter turns up in 'boat.

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the word for a boat

parts.note: a hoy is a small coastal sailing vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue, turns up means the painter's letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's stock painter

explanation.surface: An elderly artist appears aboard a small vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoary means grey or white with age, so ancient.

clue.text: Hurry, as the builder might do ?

definitions.text: Hurry, as the builder might do ?

parts.words: Hurry, as the builder might do
parts.note: a two-word phrase for hurrying read literally, as if a builder were constructing something, with making being a builder's trade

explanation.surface: Get a move on, as a busy builder would.
explanation.definitionFit: To act quickly is the idiomatic sense; the literal sense of making something suits a builder.

clue.text: Retire to make yourself this

parts.note: an idiom of going away or vanishing: you make yourself hard to find, not plentiful

explanation.surface: Withdraw, and in doing so become something you are.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'make yourself scarce' means leave or keep out of the way, which is what retiring is.

clue.text: It may be priceless, oddly enough

definitions.text: It may be priceless, oddly enough

parts.words: It may be priceless, oddly enough
parts.note: a thing beyond price is worth a great deal, odd since 'priceless' sounds as if it had no price at all

explanation.surface: Something without a price is, curiously, worth a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Priceless means worth more than can be paid, and so of great worth; the oddity is that the near-synonym looks like a negative.

clue.text: Important data displayed in attractive form ?

definitions.meaning: key figures such as births, deaths and marriages in a population
the bust, waist and hip measurements of a shapely figure

explanation.surface: Key figures set out in a pleasing way.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means essential demographic figures and, colloquially, a woman's body measurements.

clue.text: Bird needs incentive, having made a bloomer.

parts.note: the lark is a songbird
a spur is a stimulus or incentive

explanation.surface: A bird needs encouragement after making a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur is a flowering plant, so something that blooms.

clue.text: A girl upset Biblical character

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the girl's name is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: Nora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A distressed young woman, compared to someone from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Aaron was the brother of Moses and the first high priest of Israel.

clue.text: Perhaps they rescued part of Boswell's work

definitions.meaning: ropes thrown to people in danger of drowning
passages from James Boswell's Life of Samuel Johnson

explanation.surface: Perhaps a scholar saved some of a biographer's writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ropes thrown to save swimmers are lifelines; lines of Boswell's biography 'The Life of Johnson' are life lines.

clue.text: Makes start, perhaps, with supervisor

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the two words could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A manager makes things begin, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A taskmaster is someone who sets and oversees work, often severely.

clue.text: About to absorb Kipling's work-certainly not

clue.text: Fabulous trip for Tim Clay round Southend

indicators.note: round says the rearranged letters go around the next piece
a trip stumbles, so the name's letters fall into a new order

parts.note: read as South's end, the last letter of the word South

explanation.surface: Fabulous outing for a man called Tim Clay to Southend, the seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Southend is an Essex seaside resort; here it is split as 'South end', giving H. 'trip' turns TIM CLAY into MYTICAL, and 'round' puts it about H.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabulous in its older sense means belonging to fable, legendary.

clue.text: Such a woman would be missed, no doubt

definitions.text: Such a woman would be missed, no doubt

parts.words: Such a woman would be missed, no doubt
parts.note: an unmarried woman is addressed as Miss, so she would be 'Miss-ed'

explanation.surface: Her absence would surely be felt.
explanation.definitionFit: An unmarried woman is titled Miss, hence 'missed'.

clue.text: What employer does leaders of union say encourages strikes

indicators.note: leaders of means the opening letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: An employer's tactic: union heads saying they encourage strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: An employer employs staff, that is, puts them to work.

clue.text: Feeling conveyed I meant to be heartless

parts.note: conveyed means sent

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the word meant is removed

explanation.surface: Emotion was expressed, though I meant it coldly.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentiment is an attitude or emotion felt.

clue.text: Hoping to make bell sound, without corrosion

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the bell sound goes around the next piece

parts.note: ting is the light ringing of a bell
rust is corrosion of iron

explanation.surface: Hoping to make a bell ring that isn't rusty.
explanation.definitionFit: Trusting means having faith or confidence, close to hopeful expectation.

clue.text: End of matter in letters to East

indicators.note: letters suggests the words are just letters to be rearranged into a new spelling

explanation.surface: Closing a matter in letters sent eastward.
explanation.definitionFit: To terminate is to bring to a close, a verb sense of end.

clue.text: Revolutionary orchestral part in " Trees "

parts.note: a red is a revolutionary communist
the woods are the woodwind section of an orchestra

explanation.surface: A radical section of the orchestra in a piece called Trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Redwoods are huge Californian conifers.

clue.text: Like the haste of a streaker? "

definitions.text: Like the haste of a streaker?

parts.words: Like the haste of a streaker
parts.note: the idiom for unseemly hurry, applied to someone running naked, whose lack of clothes is improper

explanation.surface: How fast does a naked runner go?
explanation.definitionFit: Indecent haste is the idiom for unseemly speed; a streaker's nakedness is improper too.

clue.text: Ringleader is abroad — in a bar, perhaps

parts.note: read as the leader of the word Ring, its first letter
est is French for is

explanation.surface: The gang's ringleader is overseas, drinking in a pub somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' is a pub in the surface but a measure of music in the definition: a rest is a silence written within a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical rest is a pause marked within a measure of a score.

clue.text: Grace's favourite tree?

parts.note: W. G. Grace was the great Victorian cricketer, and cricket bats are made from this tree's wood

explanation.surface: Which tree did a woman named Grace love best?
explanation.walkthrough: Grace looks like a woman's name; it is W. G. Grace, the famous English cricketer, whose bat was made of this wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket bats are carved from a particular tree's timber, so a cricketer would favour it.

clue.text: Written when one's going to make out one's case

definitions.text: Written when one's going to make out one's case

parts.words: Written when one's going to make out one's case
parts.note: a tag filled in before travelling, to identify a suitcase, not to argue a legal case

explanation.surface: A document drawn up before arguing in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A luggage tag with name and address is written before a journey to mark a suitcase.

clue.text: Stock-farms down under — in Victoria etc

definitions.meaning: in Australia, large sheep or cattle farms
railway terminals such as London's Victoria

explanation.surface: Australian sheep farms in the state of Victoria and elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria looks like the Australian state, but it is the London railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: Australians call large ranches by this name; London's Victoria is a rail terminus.

clue.text: Her daughter-in-law was badly hurt

parts.note: the daughter-in-law in the Book of Ruth has a name that is a rearrangement of the word hurt

explanation.surface: Her son's wife was seriously injured.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible, Ruth was this woman's daughter-in-law; RUTH is an anagram of 'hurt', the 'badly' signalling the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Old Testament, the Moabite Ruth was married to a son of this widow from Bethlehem.

clue.text: Simple little man?

definitions.meaning: a simple is an old word for a medicinal plant
a short form of the name Herbert

explanation.surface: An unassuming little fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbalists call medicinal plants simples; the name is also short for Herbert.

clue.text: Speaker swallows one drink he's a beginner

indicators.note: swallows means the speaker takes the next pieces inside

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker
I is the Roman numeral for one
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A public speaker downs a drink, a novice at it.
explanation.definitionFit: An originator is someone who starts something, so its beginner.

clue.text: They carefully write catalogues for pig-farmers

parts.note: a sty is where pig-farmers keep their animals
lists are catalogues

explanation.surface: Writers who carefully draw up catalogues for pig-farmers.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylists are writers who pay close attention to the manner of their prose.

clue.text: Gamble that is making money

parts.note: a spec is a speculation, a gamble
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A gamble that brings in cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Specie is coin as opposed to paper money.
